items.project_definition: The set of properties ensuring that database transactions are processed reliably to maintain data integrity for user follows and match records.
The RESTful interface used to fetch external football data, managed via a service layer with caching and rate limiting.
A security mechanism implemented to prevent unauthorized commands from being transmitted from a user the web application trusts.
The styling layer implemented via a utility-first approach for rapid interface development.
The unique alphanumeric identifier stored for each authenticated user to link them to followed matches.
The standard lightweight data-interchange format used for responses from external football data providers.
The binary storage format used within the relational database to handle flexible data structures from external sources.
The compact, URL-safe means of representing claims to be transferred between two parties for secure session management.
The dynamic scripting language rejected as the primary development tool in favor of a statically typed alternative.
The long-term support version of the runtime environment used to ensure stability and performance.
The library of pre-built components following Material Design guidelines for the user interface.
The industry-standard protocol for authorization used to implement third-party logins via Google, Facebook, and Apple.
The abstraction layer used to facilitate database interactions and migrations without writing raw queries.
The robust, open-source relational database engine selected for its reliability and advanced feature set.
The frontend library used to build the user interface, utilizing version 18 concurrent features and hooks.
The statically typed superset of the primary scripting language used to catch errors early and improve maintainability.
The visual layer of the application, developed using either a utility-first framework or a component library.
The frontend framework considered but rejected due to the team's existing expertise in other libraries.
